result.topic_en: Euler finishes remarks on residues of powers λ relative to P−1, then states and proves the theorem that −1 is a quadratic residue of a prime P = 2n+1 exactly when n is even.
result.transcription:
112 RESIDVA EX DIVIS. POTESTATVM
exiſtente $a$ radice primitiua pro diuiſore primo P;
vnde patet, ſi exponens $\lambda$ fuerit numerus ad $P-1$
primus, ſeriem reſiduorum fore completam; at ſi
exponens $\lambda$ ad $P-1$ non ſit primus, ac maximus
eorum communis diuiſor fuerit $=d$, tum vtique in
reſiduis non omnes numeri occurrent, ſed tot tan-
tum, vt eorum multitudo ſit $=\frac{P-1}{d}$, cuius ratio
ex hactenus allatis ſatis eſt manifeſta. Sed antequam
altiores poteſtates accuratius ſcrutemur, quasdam in-
ſignes proprietates circa reſidua quadratorum expli-
caſſe iuuabit.

Theorema.

57. Diuiſore primo poſito $P=2n+1$ in
reſiduis quadratorum occurret numerus $-1$ ſeu $2n$,
quoties $n$ fuerit numerus par; ſin autem $n$ ſit nu-
merus impar, tum $-1$ ſeu $2n$ certe non reperie-
tur in reſiduis, ſed erit non-reſiduum.

Demonſtratio.

Cum progreſſio geometrica $1, a^2, a^4, a^6, a^8$ etc.
omnia producat reſidua quadratorum, euidens eſt in
ea occurrere terminum $a^n$ ſi quidem $n$ ſit numerus
par, at ſupra vidimus poteſtatem $a^n$ ſemper dare
reſiduum $-1$ ſeu $2n$; ex quo manifeſtum eſt, quo-
ties $n$ fuerit numerus par, toties in reſiduis qua-
dratorum reperiri $-1$ ſeu $2n$, contra vero ſi $n$
fuerit impar, $2n$ ſeu $-1$ erit non-reſiduum.

Coroll.

items.quote:
ſi exponens $\lambda$ ad $P-1$ non ſit primus, ac maximus
eorum communis diuiſor fuerit $=d$, tum vtique in
reſiduis non omnes numeri occurrent, ſed tot tan-
tum, vt eorum multitudo ſit $=\frac{P-1}{d}$
items.english: If the exponent λ is not prime to P−1 and their greatest common divisor is d, then not all numbers occur among the residues, but only so many that their number is (P−1)/d.

items.quote:
Sed antequam
altiores poteſtates accuratius ſcrutemur, quasdam in-
ſignes proprietates circa reſidua quadratorum expli-
caſſe iuuabit.
items.english: But before we examine higher powers more carefully, it will help to explain some remarkable properties of the residues of squares.

items.quote:
Diuiſore primo poſito $P=2n+1$ in
reſiduis quadratorum occurret numerus $-1$ ſeu $2n$,
quoties $n$ fuerit numerus par; ſin autem $n$ ſit nu-
merus impar, tum $-1$ ſeu $2n$ certe non reperie-
tur in reſiduis, ſed erit non-reſiduum.
items.english: For a prime divisor P = 2n+1, the number −1 (or 2n) occurs among the residues of squares whenever n is even; but if n is odd, then −1 (or 2n) is certainly not found among the residues, but is a non-residue.
